Getting Help

Welcome to the spconform help and troubleshooting guide. Whether you are fitting spatial conformal prediction intervals for the first time, diagnosing empirical coverage, or interfacing custom machine learning models, this guide provides answers to common questions, error diagnoses, model integration recipes, and guidelines for reporting issues.

1. Quick Support Matrix

Need Recommended Channel Details

Model Advice & Theory GitHub Issues (Question) Questions on spatial exchangeability, choice of kernel, or sample size.
Feature Requests GitHub Issues (Enhancement) Propose new diagnostic metrics, weight kernels, or interface integrations.

2. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q1: My empirical coverage is slightly below $1 - \alpha$ (e.g. 88.5% instead of 90%). Is my model invalid?

Not necessarily. Conformal prediction guarantees valid marginal coverage in expectation: $$P\left(Y_{n+1} \in \widehat{C}(S_{n+1})\right) \ge 1 - \alpha$$ For any finite test evaluation set of size $m$, the observed empirical coverage follows a Binomial distribution $\text{Binom}(m, 1 - \alpha)$ with standard error: $$\text{SE} = \sqrt{\frac{\alpha(1 - \alpha)}{m}}$$ For example, with $m = 100$ and nominal coverage $90%$ ($\alpha = 0.10$), the standard error is $\sqrt{0.1 \times 0.9 / 100} = 0.03$ ($3%$). An observed coverage between $84%$ and $96%$ falls well within normal $95%$ binomial sampling variation. You can compute the exact binomial confidence interval via:

report <- coverage_report(out, y_test)
binom.test(round(report$coverage * length(y_test)), length(y_test), p = 1 - out$alpha)

Q2: Should I use scp_geostatistical() or scp_areal()?

  • Use scp_geostatistical() when observations have continuous coordinates $(x, y)$ or $(\text{lon}, \text{lat})$, such as weather stations, air quality sensors, or soil core samples.
  • Use scp_areal() when data are aggregated over discrete spatial units (counties, municipalities, census tracts, or lattice grid cells) where relationships are defined by an adjacency matrix $W$.

Q3: How does spatial bandwidth affect interval widths?

  • In scp_geostatistical(), weights decay as $w_i = \exp(-|s_0 - s_i|^2 / (2h^2))$.
    • A smaller $h$ restricts calibration to immediately proximate neighbors, producing localized intervals that adapt to local heteroscedasticity, but may be noisy if local data are sparse.
    • A larger $h$ borrows strength from more calibration points, yielding smoother, more stable intervals that approach standard split conformal prediction.
    • The default (bandwidth = NULL) employs the median pairwise distance heuristic, which provides a robust balance for isotropic spatial domains.

Q4: Does spconform support spatio-temporal data?

Yes. Supply t_train and t0 alongside coordinates in scp_geostatistical():

out <- scp_geostatistical(
  s_train = s_train, y_train = y_train, s0 = s_test,
  pred_fun = my_st_predictor,
  t_train = t_train, t0 = t_test,
  temporal_bandwidth = 7,  # e.g. 7 days
  alpha = 0.1
)

3. Interpreting the Diagnostic Suite (diagnose())

The diagnose() function conducts five audits on spatial prediction intervals:

diag <- diagnose(out, y_true = y_test, s_test = s_test, plot = TRUE)
print(diag)

1. Marginal Coverage & Interval Width

  • coverage: Fraction of true values falling within $[L(s_0), U(s_0)]$. Should be $\ge 1 - \alpha$.
  • mean_width vs median_width: If the mean width is substantially larger than the median, spatial outliers or high-uncertainty boundary clusters are inflating interval widths.

2. Winkler Interval Score (WIS)

A strictly proper scoring rule balancing interval sharpness and miscoverage penalties: $$\text{WIS}_\alpha(l, u, y) = (u - l) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(l - y)\mathbf{1}(y < l) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(y - u)\mathbf{1}(y > u)$$ Lower scores indicate superior predictive performance (narrower intervals with minimal violations).

3. Spatial Quadrant Stratification

Partitions the 2D spatial bounding box into $n \times n$ quadrants (default $4 \times 4 = 16$).

  • Inspect whether any specific quadrant suffers severe localized under-coverage (e.g. coverage $< 75%$).
  • Local deficits often highlight unobserved spatial covariates or sharp topographical transitions.

4. Convex Hull Boundary Proximity

Examines whether intervals near the edge of the spatial domain experience degraded coverage due to spatial extrapolation. diagnose() partitions test points into Interior vs. Boundary units.

5. Spatial Autocorrelation (Moran's $I$)

Computes Moran's $I$ on absolute conformal residuals:

  • $I \approx 0$ ($p > 0.05$): Nonconformity scores are spatially independent; local exchangeability holds well.
  • $I > 0$ ($p < 0.05$): Prediction errors cluster spatially, indicating unmodeled spatial autocorrelation in the underlying point predictor.

4. Model Integration Recipes (pred_fun)

spconform is strictly model-agnostic. The pred_fun must have the signature: function(s_train, y_train, s_new) and return a plain 1D numeric vector of length nrow(s_new).

Recipe 1: Random Forest (ranger)

library(ranger)

pred_rf <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {
  df_tr <- data.frame(x = s_train[, 1], y = s_train[, 2], target = y_train)
  df_te <- data.frame(x = s_new[, 1],   y = s_new[, 2])
  
  fit <- ranger(target ~ x + y, data = df_tr, num.trees = 100)
  predict(fit, data = df_te)$predictions
}

Recipe 2: Generalized Additive Model (mgcv::gam)

library(mgcv)

pred_gam <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {
  df_tr <- data.frame(x = s_train[, 1], y = s_train[, 2], target = y_train)
  df_te <- data.frame(x = s_new[, 1],   y = s_new[, 2])
  
  fit <- gam(target ~ s(x, y, k = 20), data = df_tr)
  as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = df_te))
}

Recipe 3: Ordinary Spatial Kriging (gstat)

library(sp)
library(gstat)

pred_kriging <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {
  sp_tr <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords = s_train, data = data.frame(y = y_train))
  sp_te <- SpatialPoints(coords = s_new)
  
  vgm_mod <- fit.variogram(variogram(y ~ 1, sp_tr), vgm("Exp"))
  krig_out <- krige(y ~ 1, sp_tr, sp_te, model = vgm_mod, debug.level = 0)
  krig_out$var1.pred
}

5. Troubleshooting Common Errors & Warnings

This section provides an exhaustive guide to diagnosing and resolving statistical, computational, and dimensional errors encountered across scp_geostatistical(), scp_areal(), and diagnose().

1. Coordinate & Dimension Mismatches

Error: s_train and s0 must have the same number of coordinate columns

  • Cause: The number of spatial coordinate dimensions differs between training and query locations (for example, passing 2D coordinates (x, y) in s_train but 3D (x, y, t) in s0).
  • Fix: Verify column counts prior to execution: 
    stopifnot(ncol(s_train) == ncol(s0))

Issue: Single-point query vector treated as 1D vector instead of 1-row matrix

  • Cause: Passing a simple coordinate vector s0 = c(50.2, 14.3) rather than a 1-row matrix or data frame.
  • Fix: Coerce single query coordinates explicitly: 
    s0 <- matrix(c(50.2, 14.3), nrow = 1)

2. Missing & Non-Finite Values (NA, NaN, Inf)

Error: s_train cannot contain NA or non-finite values or y_train contains missing values

  • Cause: Sensor dropouts, unrecorded responses, or missing spatial coordinates in training or target sets.
  • Fix: Synchronize and filter rows simultaneously before passing data to spconform: 
    valid_tr <- complete.cases(s_train, y_train)
s_train  <- s_train[valid_tr, , drop = FALSE]
y_train  <- y_train[valid_tr]

valid_te <- complete.cases(s0)
s0       <- s0[valid_te, , drop = FALSE]

3. Custom Predictor (pred_fun) Return Types & Single-Row Drops

Error: pred_fun must return a numeric vector of length nrow(s_new)

  • Cause 1 (Type Mismatch): Your model's predict() method returns a matrix with 1 column, a data.frame, or an object with custom attributes rather than an atomic numeric vector.
  • Fix 1: Always wrap the return value in as.numeric(): 
    pred_fun <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {
  fit <- ranger(y ~ ., data = data.frame(s_train, y = y_train))
  as.numeric(predict(fit, data = data.frame(s_new))$predictions)
}
  • Cause 2 (Single-Row Dimension Drop): Subsetting s_new[i, ] inside pred_fun drops a 1-row matrix to a vector, causing downstream matrix multiplications or feature extractors to fail.
  • Fix 2: Always include drop = FALSE in internal subsetting operations: 
    s_sub <- s_new[idx, , drop = FALSE]

4. Coordinate Reference System (CRS) & Distance Scale Discrepancies

Symptom: Prediction intervals are excessively wide or bandwidth estimation is degenerate

  • Cause: Mixing unprojected geographic coordinates (degrees of longitude and latitude) with planar coordinates (UTM meters), or passing coordinates where axes have wildly disparate scales. In unprojected coordinates, Euclidean distance fails to account for earth curvature.
  • Fix: Reproject coordinates to a conformal planar projection (e.g. UTM or EPSG:3857) prior to calibration: 
    # Example using sf:
# pts_projected <- sf::st_transform(pts_sf, crs = 32638)
# s_train <- sf::st_coordinates(pts_projected)

5. Areal Adjacency Matrix Structural Errors

Error: adjacency must be a square numeric matrix

  • Cause: Passing a non-square matrix (nrow(adjacency) != ncol(adjacency)) or an adjacency list rather than a binary/weighted contiguity matrix.
  • Fix: Validate matrix dimensions: 
    stopifnot(is.matrix(adjacency), nrow(adjacency) == ncol(adjacency))

Warning: Effective neighbourhood weight vanishingly small; falling back to unweighted quantile

  • Cause: An areal unit has no graph neighbors in the training set (e.g. an isolated island, enclaved district, or disconnected graph component with degree zero).
  • Fix: Audit graph connectivity. Identify isolated units and bridge graph components or adjust contiguity criteria: 
    isolated <- which(rowSums(adjacency) == 0)
if (length(isolated) > 0) {
  message("Isolated units detected: ", paste(isolated, collapse = ", "))
}

6. Calibration Sample Size vs. Nominal Miscoverage ($\alpha$)

Symptom: Conformal quantile returns the maximum nonconformity score or upper bound is uninformative

  • Cause (Mathematical Degeneracy): The held-out calibration set is too small for the requested miscoverage level $\alpha$. Conformal prediction requires: $$N_{\text{cal}} \ge \left\lceil \frac{1 - \alpha}{\alpha} \right\rceil$$ For example, requesting a 99% interval ($\alpha = 0.01$) when $N_{\text{cal}} = 40$ mathematically cannot calibrate a 99% empirical quantile, as the highest empirical quantile available is $1 - 1/(N_{\text{cal}} + 1) = 97.6%$.
  • Fix: Either increase the calibration partition size via split (e.g. split = 0.5 instead of 0.8), or choose an $\alpha$ commensurate with sample size (e.g. $\alpha = 0.05$ or $0.10$).

7. Evaluation & Diagnostic Alignment

Error: y_true must have the same length as object$pred

  • Cause: Passing the entire response vector y instead of the held-out evaluation subset corresponding to s0.
  • Fix: Align evaluation indices: 
    # Correct evaluation subset:
coverage_report(out, y_true = y_test)
diagnose(out, y_true = y_test, s_test = s_test)

Error: s_test is required for spatial stratification and boundary audits

  • Cause: Calling diagnose(out, y_true = y_test) without providing query coordinates s_test. Without coordinates, diagnose() cannot compute spatial quadrant partitions, convex hull boundaries, or Moran's $I$.
  • Fix: Always provide s_test: 
    diag <- diagnose(out, y_true = y_test, s_test = s_test, plot = TRUE)

8. Graphics Layout & Multi-Panel Plot Devices

Warning: Plot margins too large or layout display clipped in RStudio

  • Cause: The multi-panel diagnostic plot (diagnose()) renders 4 to 6 visual audits simultaneously, requiring adequate display geometry.
  • Fix: Open an expanded graphic window before plotting, or extract numerical diagnostics without plotting: 
    # Numerical diagnostics only (no graphical device):
diag <- diagnose(out, y_true = y_test, s_test = s_test, plot = FALSE)
print(diag)

# For plotting, expand display device:
dev.new(width = 11, height = 7)
plot(diag)

6. Submitting a Minimal Reproducible Example (reprex)

If you encounter unexpected behavior, please create a self-contained reproducible example:

library(spconform)

# 1. Synthetic reproducible dataset
set.seed(42)
n_tr <- 80
n_te <- 20
s_train <- matrix(runif(n_tr * 2), ncol = 2)
y_train <- sin(3 * s_train[, 1]) + rnorm(n_tr, sd = 0.2)

s_test  <- matrix(runif(n_te * 2), ncol = 2)
y_test  <- sin(3 * s_test[, 1])  + rnorm(n_te, sd = 0.2)

# 2. Simple baseline predictor
pfun <- function(s_tr, y_tr, s_new) {
  rep(mean(y_tr), nrow(s_new))
}

# 3. Execution triggering the issue
out <- scp_geostatistical(s_train, y_train, s_test, pfun, alpha = 0.1)
cov <- coverage_report(out, y_test)
print(cov)

# 4. Environment details
sessionInfo()
